problem: Standard distributed RL uses asynchronous rollout workers and a central parameter server. This design fits cheap CPU environments such as Atari and Gym, but not GPU-accelerated 3D simulators with ResNet-scale policies. As a result, prior PointGoalNav agents were trained for only 5M–75M steps, well short of saturation. Whether PointGoalNav with GPS+Compass is fully learnable remained open.
motivation: Savva et al. (2019) showed that learning-based agents overtook classical map-and-plan once training went from 5M to 75M steps, and performance still had not saturated. That raised the question of the task's fundamental learnability limit. Answering it needs orders of magnitude more experience. That in turn requires a distributed RL scheme that scales near-linearly on GPU-heavy, heterogeneous simulators and is simple to implement.
key_idea: Adapt synchronous data-parallel training (AllReduce of gradients, no parameter server) to on-policy PPO, where each GPU worker both simulates and optimizes. Add a preemption threshold that cuts straggler rollouts short once p% of workers have finished. This lets PointGoalNav agents be trained for 2.5B frames, which essentially 'solves' RGB-D + GPS+Compass PointGoalNav.
insight: Synchronous decentralized training with straggler preemption scales near-linearly on both workloads tested. Homogeneous Gibson workloads reach a 196x speedup on 256 GPUs. Heterogeneous Gibson+MP3D workloads scale poorly with no preemption (100%) but match homogeneous scaling at 60–80% thresholds, with no loss in the learned policy. With that scale, PointGoalNav performance keeps improving past 1B steps. The error-vs-compute curve looks like a power law: 90% of peak is reached at 100M steps, suggesting prior studies stopped 1–2 orders of magnitude too early. The data ablations (Tab. 1) show two things. First, adding poorly reconstructed Gibson-2/3 scenes improves val SPL from 0.922 to 0.956, likely by making representations more robust. Second, larger encoders and LSTMs add +0.003 and +0.010 SPL. A Blind (GPS+Compass-only) agent does well on short episodes but drops to about 0.3 SPL (vs 0.95 for RGB-D) at 20–25m. So layout regularities explain short-range success, while depth provides the signal for long-range navigation.
method: DD-PPO synchronous data-parallel RL: each GPU worker alternates between (a) collecting on-policy rollouts from 4 local environments, batched for inference, and (b) PPO optimization. Gradients are AllReduced via PyTorch DistributedDataParallel (NCCL), with no parameter server and no stale computation.

Straggler preemption: a TCPStore key-value counter tracks how many workers have finished collecting. Once more than p% have finished (60% works well), remaining workers stop their rollouts early. A minimum of 1/4 of the max steps is enforced, and all workers' losses are weighted equally.

Agent architecture: visual encoder is a half-width ResNet50, SE-ResNeXt50 or SE-ResNeXt101. It uses a 2x2 AvgPool front (effective 128x128 input), GroupNorm instead of BatchNorm, and outputs a 1024x4x4 map, reduced to 128x4x4 by a 3x3 conv. The goal vector [d, cos θ, sin θ] is embedded to 32-d by an FC layer, and the previous action to a 32-d embedding.

Policy: a 2-layer LSTM (512-d or 1024-d hidden) takes the flattened visual features (FC to hidden size), the goal embedding and the previous-action embedding, and outputs a softmax over 4 actions plus a value estimate.

Training: PPO+GAE (γ=0.99, τ=0.95), 128-step rollouts x 4 envs per worker, 2 epochs x 2 minibatches, Adam lr 2.5e-4, no advantage normalization. Reward is terminal 2.5·SPL plus shaped −Δgeodesic distance − 0.01 per step. Training runs on 64 V100s for 2.5B steps (≈180 GPU-days, 2.75 days wall-clock).

Training-data scaling: Gibson-4+ (72 challenge scenes) → +all 90 Matterport3D scenes → Gibson-2+ (332 train scenes including poorly reconstructed meshes). RGB agents use channel-wise input normalization and Gibson-2+ plus MP3D.

Transfer (secondary): the PointGoalNav encoder/policy is reused for Flee and Exploration (frozen encoder, fine-tuned policy). A '∇ Neural Controller' variant trains an LSTM planner that emits point goals and backpropagates through the frozen differentiable navigator.

setting.backbone: SE-ResNeXt101 (half-width, GroupNorm) visual encoder + 2-layer 1024-d LSTM policy, trained from scratch with RL. Variants: ResNet50 / SE-ResNeXt50 + 512-d LSTM.
setting.training_data: RL in Habitat for 2.5B steps. Best model uses Gibson-2+ (332 Gibson train scenes rated ≥2). Variants use Gibson-4+ (72 Habitat Challenge 2019 train scenes) and Gibson-4+ plus all 90 Matterport3D scenes (including MP3D val/test). The RGB agent uses Gibson-2+ plus all MP3D.
setting.observation: egocentric 256x256 Depth (RGB-D agent uses Depth only) or RGB, plus GPS+Compass (goal relative to current pose); Blind variant uses GPS+Compass only
setting.action_space: discrete: STOP, MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN_LEFT 10°, TURN_RIGHT 10°
setting.privileged: Noise-free GPS+Compass sensor, part of the Habitat Challenge 2019 PointGoalNav spec. Geodesic-distance shaped reward is used only at training time. No map at test time.

results: The best RGB-D agent (SE-ResNeXt101 + 1024-d LSTM, Gibson-2+, 2.5B steps) reaches 0.969 SPL / 0.997 success on Habitat Challenge 2019 val and 0.948 SPL / 0.980 success on test-std. That sets the state of the art on the RGB-D track, within 3–5% of the shortest-path oracle. It also beats the classical map-and-plan baseline (0.92 val / 0.89 test SPL). The RGB agent improves from 0.57/0.47 SPL (Savva et al. 2019 PPO) to 0.929 val / 0.920 test SPL with about 99% success, leading the RGB track (rank-2 entry 0.89 SPL). DD-PPO scales near-linearly, and PointGoalNav-pretrained encoders transfer to Flee and Exploration better than ImageNet-pretrained ones.
limitations: The 'solved' claim depends on a perfect, noise-free GPS+Compass. Without it (RGB only), the agent reaches just 0.15 SPL after 2.5B steps. Everything is simulation-only, with no real-robot validation.
Needs massive compute: 2.5B frames ≈ 180 GPU-days on 64 V100s. About 90% of peak is reachable at 100M steps (~1 day on 8 GPUs).

Remaining failures: slight stair traversal (the GPS is 2D), mesh holes that act as 'sink' locations, and episodes with a high geodesic/Euclidean distance ratio. The method is validated only with on-policy PPO.
